items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: I went back and dialed up the Ink Spots’ record and there was Jimmy Blythe’s little opener.

ctx.x: It’s funny how things turn out like that. I’m going to — this is a tough question perhaps — can you remember the first recorded music that you heard that sort of struck a nerve with you, that made your ears perk up?

I can’t remember not liking music at all or not responding to it. I guess sort of an answer to your question is what are my earliest music memories and there’s one that really sticks out. I was born in 1937 so I would have been four I think when I heard the Ink Spots I guess it was, singing “I Don’t Want to Set the World on Fire.” I didn’t respond to the Ink Spots so much as to the idea of arson, and the whole planet going up and at age four when people say things like that you hear them literally. So I remember…

Spots’ record and there was Jimmy Blythe’s little opener. So they ripped that off from him, right? Or at least it was around in community folklore section, it was available to the Ink Spots fifteen years after Ma Rainey and Jimmy Blythe picked it up. I thought that was nice. And so I was listening to music carefully when I was only four years old.
